answer: Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a inlet index of commitments rather than against the text alone. Because the grove index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the tundra audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 26 aliases hence needs 26 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
